title: The Real Reason You Procrastinate (It's Not Laziness)
description:
You are not lazy. Procrastination is an emotion regulation problem, not a time management problem. In this video we break down why your brain avoids hard tasks, what the amygdala has to do with it, and the 10-second rule that actually works.

00:00 The laziness myth
01:10 Why your brain avoids discomfort
02:35 The 10-second rule
03:50 What to do tomorrow morning

scenes.narration: You are not lazy. If you were lazy, you would not feel guilty about putting things off. The fact that you care is proof that something else is going on.
Procrastination is not a time management problem. It is an emotion regulation problem. Your brain is not avoiding the work. It is avoiding the bad feeling the work produces.

When you think about a hard task, your amygdala fires up. It reads the task as a threat, floods you with mild stress, and your brain reaches for anything that makes that feeling stop. Usually that thing is your phone.

Here is the part nobody tells you. The relief you get from delay is real, but it lasts about six seconds. Then the guilt comes back, stronger than before, and now you are fighting two problems instead of one.
The fix is embarrassingly small. Pick the single task that scares you most. Set a timer for ten seconds. And start. Not finish. Start. Momentum is the only thing your brain actually needs.
Do that for one week and the shame loop breaks. You were never broken. You were just managing feelings instead of minutes.
